narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Whirl of Bohemia
This is redowa. 19th century.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Title card: redowa · Czech Republic · 19th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The dance originated in Bohemia as the rejdovák.
It transitioned from a rural folk dance to the salons of Prague in 1829.
It reached London by 1846 and was widely practiced in the United States and France by the 1850s.
on_screen: Map: Czech Republic · Europe
Image 1 with attribution

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Originally a social ballroom dance for the 19th-century elite, it transitioned into a folk dance in Mexico, where it is now performed at festivals and by traditional dance groups.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Nikolaj Rimskij-Korsakov, SUITE D'OPERA - Richard Kapp, Milton Katims, David Zinman (https://archive.org/details/rimsky-korsakov-opera-suites)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The redowa is performed in a closed waltz position.
The basic step consists of a six-count pattern: a long reaching step followed by two small leap-steps.
The leader and follower perform opposite sequences, rotating clockwise.
Watch for Pursuit.
on_screen: Hero video — MISSING
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couple dance moving in a line of direction.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is written in 3/4 time.
It is described as having a slower tempo than the standard waltz or polka-mazurka.
Listen for the accordion, bajo sexto.
The pulse is 3/4.
A 3/4 time dance music that is slower than a standard waltz, characterized by a distinct rhythmic accentuation.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned
Listen later: El naranjo — Antonio Tanguma Guajardo
Waveform or rhythm-pattern graphic: Six-beat rotation pattern

scenes.title: The people
narration: Henri Cellarius, a 19th-century dance master, and Antonio Tanguma Guajardo, a Mexican composer of redovas.
The European salon redowa, which largely vanished, and the Mexican redova, which persists as a traditional folk dance in northern states.
Derived from the Czech rejdovák, it is a sibling to the polka and mazurka, and a parent to the Mexican redova.
